full_text:
Rialo：革新区块链与现实世界的连接方式

@RialoHQ  作为一个面向现实世界的区块链平台应运而生。它的目标是打破区块链与现实世界之间的壁垒，使开发团队能够像开发Web2应用一样轻松地构建可用于生产环境的区块链应用程序。Rialo希望将区块链技术像智能手机一样无缝融入人们的日常生活。

Rialo 是什么？
Rialo 是由 @Subzero_Labs   专为现实世界开发的区块链，但其定位跳出了过往的 Layer1、Layer2 或 Layer3 框架，全称为「Rialo isn’t a layer 1」。

用 Subzero Labs 联合创始人 Ade Adepoju 在《财富》杂志上的比喻：「这就像当年 iPod 到 iPhone 的进化 —— 我们不需要另一个只能听歌的设备，而是需要一个能整合相机、网络、GPS 的全能工具。”

Rialo 的核心目标是降低区块链的使用门槛，让非加密领域的开发者也能轻松构建应用。它最显著的特点是「原生连接现实世界」：例如，开发者可以直接在智能合约中调用网页信息（如 FICO 信用分），无需依赖第三方预言机；用户可以用社交账号、邮箱等熟悉的身份登录，无需从零开始学习钱包操作。

Fabric Ventures 解释其为何投资 Rialo 时表示，Rialo 通过将现实世界开发者所需的核心功能嵌入协议本身，改变了区块链 L1 的侧重点。调用、数据流、 timers 和跨链操作都变成了原生指令，而非依赖外呼。预言机、跨链桥、索引器和其他「传统」基础设施可能不再有必要。

团队和融资背景
8 月初，Subzero Labs 宣布完成 2000 万美元种子轮融资，Pantera Capital 领投，Coinbase 等参投。据财富杂志，CEO Ade Adepoju 表示，这笔融资于今年一季度完成，涉及股权和代币认股权证。

Subzero Labs 团队成员曾任职于 Meta、Apple、Amazon、Netflix、Google、TikTok、Citadel、Mysten Labs、Solana 等公司或项目，在区块链、人工智能、分布式系统和硬件领域拥有比较丰富的经验。

·  联合创始人兼 CEO Ade Adepoju (@itachee_x )：曾在多家科技公司担任工程师职务。2021年底加入加密领域，参与了Mysten Labs区块链项目的早期开发。

·  联合创始人兼 CTO Lu Zhang（ @firearrowmage ）：曾任 Mysten Labs 工程师。

Rialo 如何运行？
虽然 Rialo 尚未完全披露其区块链架构，但从公开信息来看，其运行逻辑主要围绕以下关键点展开：

1.结合 RISC-V 和 Solana VM 兼容性：Rialo 的智能合约运行时称为 ThruVM，它实现了开放的 RISC-V 规范，支持与现有 Rust、C 等语言兼容，同时兼容 Solana VM 以提升性能和开发友好度。

2.降低摩擦和原生整合：项目强调人体工程学设计（ergonomic），使非加密开发者更容易构建去中心化、高性能的应用，与现实生活互动（如现实世界资产 RWA 在区块链上的应用）。它旨在从混乱转向统一，提供无缝的链上-链下集成。

3.去中心化和高性能：作为一个模块化 L1 网络，Rialo 聚焦于现实世界应用的编程网络，支持现实资产在区块链上的“活化”，并通过全栈系统避免传统区块链的碎片化问题。

Rialo 的未来展望
总之，Rialo 不仅仅是一个区块链项目，更是区块链技术向现实世界迈进的关键一步。通过其创新的架构和开发者友好的设计，Rialo 有望重塑加密生态，让更多传统行业的从业者参与其中，推动 Web3 的真正大众化。我们期待 Rialo 能在 2025 年及以后，成为连接数字与物理世界的桥梁。

Rialo: The Invisible Infrastructure Redefining Blockchain Adoption

In the world of cryptocurrencies, where innovation is often measured by technical complexity, @RialoHQ  emerges as a paradigm of radical simplicity. It is not a conventional Layer 1, that rigid architecture that prioritizes scalability over usability, but a hybrid system that merges the roles of client and network into a single, fluid entity.

This flexibility allows not only efficient transactions but also intelligent automation. Imagine Rialo executing a trade on your behalf or resolving local settlements without manual intervention, all happening seamlessly in the background 🤯

The philosophical core of Rialo lies in its rejection of the barriers that have slowed the mass adoption of cryptocurrencies. Outside of CT circles, most real-world users still see blockchains as a maze of seed phrases and private keys. Rialo reverses this logic: instead of forcing users to adapt to the technology, the technology adapts to everyday routines.

It is the thesis of invisible infrastructure, comparable to how Amazon Web Services (AWS) powers Netflix streaming without the viewer ever realizing it. There are no alerts interrupting the flow, only pure functionality.

But Rialo goes beyond accessibility. Its architecture incorporates bidirectional APIs that enable fluid interaction from any interface: chat directly with the network on X, send commands via traditional messaging, or integrate actions into trusted applications. It requires no additional apps or external services, everything is built into the protocol itself.

Ultimately, Rialo not only solves technical problems but also anticipates a future where cryptocurrencies stop being a novelty and become an everyday tool.

1/🧵What is @RialoHQ ?

Rialo is a blockchain built for the real world.

Not just fast. Not just decentralized. Rialo is designed to feel like modern software: seamless, reactive, and intuitive.

Let’s break it down 👇

1️⃣Bitcoin gave us digital scarcity. Ethereum introduced programmable trust. Then came fast chains chasing TPS. But users still quit early. Why?

Because Web3 apps feel clunky, slow, and disconnected. Too many steps. Too little reliability.

2️⃣Rialo is a fresh start.
A decentralized, high-performance programming network that interacts with real life—like Uber, Instagram, or WhatsApp did for mobile.

It’s not just a chain. It’s a convergence point.

3️⃣Rialo solves the real problems:
▪️ Switching networks and juggling wrapped tokens 
▪️ Wallet UX nightmares and endless signing 
▪️ Unpredictable fees and sandwich attacks 
▪️ Losing your social identity when you go onchain 
▪️ No 2FA, no scheduled transactions, no sleep

4️⃣For developers, it’s even worse:
▪️ 10% coding, 90% integrations 
▪️ Slow reads, stale data 
▪️ Fragile bots and off-chain monitors 
▪️ Expensive indexers and oracle fees 
▪️ Bridges that weaken your trust model

5️⃣Rialo flips the script
It’s not performance theater. It’s performance that matters.
Built from the ground up to be ergonomic, reactive, and deeply connected to the real world.

6️⃣Real-world capabilities, natively onchain:
• Real Data: Pull live data with a one-liner HTTPS call 
• Real Identity: Use email, SMS, or social logins 
• Real Privacy: Verifiable + confidential execution 
• Real Speed: Sub-second latency, end-to-end 
• Real Reactivity: Instant onchain triggers, no bots 
• Real Programmability: Sleep, loop, resume, fully onchain 
• Real Usability: 2FA, scheduled txs, social logins 
• Real Assets: Mainstream + long-tail, effortlessly 
• Real Applications: Beyond speculation

7️⃣Rialo is supermodular.
Each capability amplifies the others. Together, they create a system where the whole is far greater than the sum of its parts.
Apps become simpler, faster, and more capable, by default.

8️⃣Rialo’s DevNet is live.
Join elite builders, early adopters, and real-world apps pushing boundaries.

full_text:
Grialo indonesia

Berikut adalah beberapa poin utama (highlight) dari sesi community sharing Rialo Indonesia, yang dipimpin oleh Regional Helper @kgufranp  dan @0x_vibevortex . Sesi ini membahas update komunitas, peran helper, dan diskusi Q&A dengan peserta:

1. Peran dan Fungsi Regional Helper
Sebagai Jembatan: Tugas utama regional helper adalah menjadi penghubung antara komunitas regional (Indonesia) dengan tim inti @RialoHQ  di Discord.

- Menerima Aspirasi: Mereka menampung masukan, inspirasi, dan kritik konstruktif dari anggota komunitas untuk disampaikan ke tim.

- Bukan Pemberi Role : Regional helper menegaskan bahwa mereka tidak memiliki wewenang untuk memberikan atau merekomendasikan role secara langsung. Keputusan akhir tetap ada di tim (seperti Orca).

- Bekerja Sama : Mereka menekankan bahwa status helper bukanlah tingkatan, melainkan peran untuk memajukan komunitas. Mereka tetap berkontribusi seperti anggota lainnya.

-------------

2. Perubahan Besar pada Komunitas dan Role
Fokus pada "Komunitas, Bukan Farmer": Tim Rialo (khususnya founder, @itachee_x ) ingin mengubah citra komunitas dari yang terlihat seperti "tempat farming" role menjadi komunitas yang benar-benar membangun.

- Penghapusan Role: Banyak role seperti Rialoyal, Builder, dan Rialorbit telah dihapus. Alasannya, sistem role sebelumnya dianggap terlalu banyak dan mendorong mental "farming".

- Perombakan Server Discord: Nama server dan beberapa channel diubah untuk mendukung visi komunitas yang baru.

- Role Baru Akan Datang: Akan ada role-role baru untuk para kontributor di bidang tertentu, seperti Artis, Trader, dan Pembuat Meme, meski detailnya masih belum final.

-------------

3. Sistem Club Member dan PURS
- Club Member adalah Identitas: Role Rialo Club Member saat ini lebih difokuskan sebagai penanda "jati diri" bahwa seseorang adalah bagian dari klub.

- PURS (Pull/Remove System): Sistem ini akan terus berjalan untuk mengevaluasi keaktifan member club. Member yang tidak aktif berisiko dicabut role-nya.

- Seleksi Semakin Ketat: Kedepannya, proses seleksi untuk menjadi Club Member akan semakin sulit dan selektif. Mereka yang sudah menjadi member diingatkan untuk tetap aktif dan berkontribusi secara bermakna.

-------------

4. Pembaruan Produk dan Teknis
- Visi Rialo: Rialo digambarkan sebagai "iPhone-nya crypto" yang bertujuan menjembatani Web2 dan Web3, mengintegrasikan aplikasi seperti X, Instagram, dan SMS ke dalam blockchain.

- Fokus pada RWA (Real World Assets): Rialo berfokus pada aset dunia nyata, namun dengan cakupan yang luas, tidak hanya infrastruktur tetapi juga hak intelektual, dll.

- Kesempatan untuk Builder: Bagi developer, terdapat form submission untuk membangun proyek (DeFi, AI, Gaming, dll) di ekosistem Rialo. Untuk akses API key dan dukungan teknis lainnya, tim masih akan mengklarifikasi lebih lanjut.

- Roadmap Belum Rilis: Roadmap resmi proyek belum dirilis karena tim masih melakukan perombakan besar-besaran.

-------------

5. Pesan Penting untuk Komunitas
- Proyek Masih Sangat Awal (Early): Tim menekankan bahwa Rialo masih dalam tahap sangat awal dan meminta komunitas untuk bersabar dan fokus membangun dalam jangka panjang.

- Kontribusi yang Berkualitas: Anggota didorong untuk berkontribusi dengan kualitas, bukan kuantitas. Diskusi yang bermakna lebih dihargai daripada sekadar chat "good morning" atau pertanyaan tentang role.

- Hindari Fokus Berlebihan pada Role: Terlalu sering membahas dan mempertanyakan role dikhawatirkan akan menjadi bumerang dan justru membuat tim semakin ketat dalam seleksi.

- Belum Masuk Kaito: Rialo saat ini memilih untuk fokus membangun komunitas internal terlebih dahulu dan belum berencana untuk terintegrasi dengan platform seperti Kaito.

full_text:
Bonds in the New Era: Rialo and the Transformation of Global Economic Dynamics

In the ever-changing global economic landscape, bonds play a vital role as a funding instrument for governments and corporations. However, interest rate volatility, volatile inflation, and geopolitical turmoil make the traditional bond market increasingly vulnerable. full_text:
Rialo vs traditional oracles 🧵 (part 1)

most chains still lean on oracles like chainlink for offchain data, but rialo just.. doesn't. lets break it down, because the difference could actually fix some real dev pain.

First, quick reminder:

traditional oracles (chainlink, band, etc.) are these decentralized networks of nodes that fetch real world data.. like prices, weather, or api feeds.., and pipe it onchain. smart contracts request it, nodes compete to deliver, reaches agreement.. then provide usable data. this powers defi tvl in the billions, because without it, we'd have no lending or perps.

but all this is still middleware. you open a dapp, pay fees per request, deal with latency (even if sub-second), and trust the network won't get manipulated or go down. devs waste time wiring it up, and for such simple stuff, it feels like using a sledgehammer for a nail.

Rialo comes in.. no oracles needed, because web connectivity is baked in natively.

Contracts make direct https calls to apis, pull live data (weather, cpi, payments, whatever), and verify it right onchain.

Validators monitor public sources as triggers.. imagine

if a tweet goes viral, it auto triggers a payout or a delivery webhook settles an invoice instantly

it's event driven from the ground up; transactions are executed on timers, webhooks, or real events, without much latency. no polling bots, no third-party dependencies.

Like one post put it, "rialo skips all that... apps that stay up to date automatically as outside data changes.

⚡How onchain RWAs are brought to life by @RialoHQ:

Today's tokenized Real World Assets are limited and they also depend heavily on off-chain verification, are slow to respond to real world events.

full_text:
The most interesting thing about @RialoHQ  is how cause and effect are wired together. The world says something, the network hears it, the contract responds. Not a bot, not an intermediate service, not let’s poll in a minute, but a clean line: an event happens, code runs, state changes. At that point the blockchain stops pretending to be a middleman and starts behaving like automation. It sounds simple, but in practice it changes decisions almost everywhere.

How it feels from the inside: a contract doesn’t live in fetch me data on a schedule mode. It lives in a system where data arrives when there’s a reason. On the outside, it’s familiar stuffwebhooks, HTTP endpoints, signals from payment services or delivery tracking, even weather providers. On the inside, it’s well-formed events with clear provenance and boundaries: where it came from, when it arrived, what exactly happened. The network picks up the signal and starts the right piece of code. After that, it’s just contract logic. I once watched innocent polling break risk management because a bot woke up three minutes late. Here that kind of story is rarer: the reaction is tied to the fact, not the timer.

Going out to the web doesn’t look like a hack. When a contract needs to check a payment status or pull a fact from the web, it does it as part of the scenario, not through a backroom deal with a private backend. The decision happens when it should: a payment lands and the deal moves forward; rainfall is recorded and an insurance payout is computed; delivery is confirmed and obligations close while collateral unlocks. There isn’t a six-layer glue stack you can’t debug later. And when something does break , you can see it in the big picture: where a timeout happened, which signal was duplicated, what exactly the contract ignored thanks to idempotency.

Discipline at the edges is non-negotiable. Reactive systems don’t work without verifiable sources. Events need a signature or some way to prove origin; external domains need an explicit allowlist; handlers need protection against duplicates and replays. It’s not magic, it’s the boring engineering: timeouts, retries, deduplication, backpressure, clear delivery guarantees. What you lose is the old story: some VPS container died, nobody noticed, the market moved. Here those things become visible instead of hiding in the shadows.

There’s another practical win: code portability. From their materials, SVM-level execution support means you don’t have to start from zero you can bring existing programs and familiar patterns. Not a cure-all, sure, but it lowers friction: less rewriting, more focus on the scenario itself event, then behavior. And yes, speed and latency matter, but here they’re a consequence of the model, not the headline goal.

Rialo’s chain behaves like an event bus, and contracts behave like subscribers with clear rules. Cause and effect line up into one conveyor, where happened almost immediately means handled. The ledger still records facts, but it grows a reflex. Less noisy infrastructure around it, more understandable logic inside.

Realio Network: Operation "Tokenization of the Mainland"
Department of RWA (Real-World Assets): Realio Network is a specialized Layer—1 blockchain, whose mission is to "digitize physical evidence" (real-world assets such as real estate and private equity) and bring them from the traditional world to the jurisdiction of Web3.

Double Agent (RIO and RST Tokens): The network uses a dual token model to ensure legality: RIO acts as a "Universal Token" for payment of commissions and management, and RST acts as an "Official Document" (regulated security token) representing a share of the capital, which is critical for institutional compliance.

Real-World Privacy: Applications can send encrypted messages directly to real people—via email, phone, or device ID—without requiring a wallet setup. This makes communication secure by default.

What is Rialo’s Technical Vision
@RialoHQ is being built by Subzero Labs as a “real-world blockchain” meant to reduce friction between Web3 apps and everyday users. They see current apps as too clunky too many middleware layers, oracles, identity friction, etc. They want to bring real-world usability to blockchain.
Some of Rialo’s core tech promises include:

1) Native web connectivity / real-world data: Smart contracts should be able to do one-line HTTPS calls, integrate off-chain APIs directly. No heavy dependency on third-party oracle systems.
2) Event-driven transactions & reactivity: Contracts that trigger based on real-world events, timers, etc. Think Web2 paradigms of event listeners + asynchronous behavior brought into blockchain. 
3) Architecture & compatibility: Rialo aims to be compatible with RISC-V smart contracts architecture and Solana VM compatibility. This means: using an open instruction set (RISC-V) for contract execution, plus compatibility so that things built for Solana VM or using similar tooling could be easier to port or adapt.

How Rialo Intends to Do It (Mechanics & Challenges)
1) Developer-first design: They want the infrastructure to feel familiar to Web2 devs. That means simpler identity systems (email, SMS, social login), built-in transaction scheduling, predictable fees, user triggers, etc. Reduce the learning curve.
2) Real-world integrations baked in: Instead of building oracles and middleware for each new data source or service, Rialo aims to have many real-world capabilities built into the protocol. For example, pulling in data like credit scores, weather, payments info, etc., directly and safely.
3) Privacy & predictability: They’re focusing on fast transactions, stable/affordable fees, privacy / confidentiality options, predictable UX (less surprise gas fees, more dependable response times).
4) Not strictly a classic Layer-1: Rialo positions itself as more than traditional L1, L2 or 3. It’s rethinking what blockchain should natively support so that many pieces that are optional elsewhere (identity, API access, event triggers) are first-class.

full_text:
The issues with Web3 adoption after 16 years boil down mainly to user experience (UX), complexity, and inflexibility in current blockchain infrastructures. While Bitcoin established digital scarcity, Ethereum introduced programmable trust, and blockchains like Solana delivered high transaction throughput, mainstream adoption still struggles because:
->Wallets are complex and inconvenient, requiring users to sign many transactions daily, leading to fatigue.
->Bridges between chains are risky and complicated, creating security fears.
->Transaction fees vary unpredictably, causing frustration.
->Security incidents and hacks discourage new users.
->The overall experience feels more like a technical grind than a seamless product, causing many "normies" to try once and quit.

@RialoHQ ’s pitch addresses these deep pain points by fundamentally rebuilding the blockchain experience from the ground up rather than patching legacy chains. Key innovations are:
»Native webcalls: Contracts can directly fetch any real-world API data (weather, CPI, payments) inside themselves, removing middleware like oracles.
»Real-world identity integration: Users log in with social accounts, email, SMS making onboarding smooth and familiar.
»Programmable, event-driven contracts: Contracts can wait, sleep, or respond instantly to live external events, enabling automation and real-time asset management.
»Sub-second latency and infinite scalability through multiple concurrent proposers.
»User-friendly features like 2FA and social recovery integrated on-chain.
»Privacy layers for verifiable yet confidential executions.
»A supermodular design combining data feeds, reactivity, and identity creates “living apps” that react instantly and automatically to real-world inputs.

@RialoHQ ’s vision of “real-world assets” solves the common issue of tokenized assets being static digital representations. For example:

->Bonds that update yield dynamically based on CPI.
->Invoices that auto-settle when payments are confirmed by Stripe.
->Cargo insurance releasing funds automatically on GPS confirmation.
->Perishable goods contracts canceling if IoT sensors detect spoilage.
This represents a shift from “static PDFs on chain” to actively responsive “living assets”.

For users, Rialo aims to turn crypto apps into experiences as natural as Instagram or WhatsApp, such as:
->Instantly tipping an Instagram creator.
->Insurance paying out automatically for flight delays.
->Telegram group raffles settling instantly on-chain.
->Live royalty splits on Spotify streams without multi-month waits.

For developers, building on Rialo avoids the “Rube Goldberg machine” of stitching together oracles, keepers, relayers, and cron jobs seen in other chains. Rialo integrates native automation, direct HTTP calls, event-driven execution, and supports RISC-V and Solana virtual machines for versatile development. This shortening of development cycles from months to days is designed to accelerate innovation and usability.

In summary, Web3 adoption struggles because existing chains prioritize benchmarks like TPS over real-world usability, suffer from UX friction, security fears, and static asset models. Rialo responds by reimagining blockchain as a seamless, reactive, real-world-connected system with identity and privacy, enabling instant, familiar, and automated interactions for users and simpler powerful tools for developers. This might finally deliver the “iPhone moment” for Web3, turning it from a niche crypto sandbox into everyday, practical apps.This explains the detailed narrative and vision behind Rialo’s approach to overcoming the most persistent problems in Web3 adoption.

#RWA #Rialo

Current Existing Blockchains V/S Rialo

@RialoHQ is a next-generation blockchain designed to bridge the gap between Web2 and Web3 by creating a seamless connection with the real world. Unlike existing blockchains, which often feel clunky, slow, and isolated from everyday user experiences, Rialo aims to offer a decentralized, high-performance network that interacts directly with real-life data and services, enabling more intuitive and reliable decentralized applications (dapps).

What Went Wrong with Current Blockchains ?

Current blockchains focus on metrics like transactions per second (TPS) but fail to solve deeper user and developer problems:
->Users face complicated network switching, fragmented wallets, unpredictable fees, and loss of social identities.
->Developers struggle with complex third-party integrations, slow data propagation, costly infrastructure, and insecure bridges.
These issues stem from blockchains being isolated "islands" without true connectivity to real-world services or user-friendly designs.

Rialo's Approach and Features

Rialo reimagines blockchain infrastructure to be clean, expressive, and connected with the real world. Key features include:
->Real World Data & Connectivity: Smart contracts can easily pull live external data and interact with off-chain APIs through simple HTTPS calls.
->Real World Identity: Allows users to use familiar credentials like email, SMS, and social accounts as Web3 passports, preserving social identities and enabling new use cases like crypto loans based on credit scores.
->Real World Speed and Scalability: Sub-second end-to-end latency and infinite scalability via multiple concurrent block proposers enable fast and global dapps.
->Real World Programmability: Event-driven logic, randomness, and advanced features like smart contracts that can sleep, loop, and resume on-chain, powered by RISC-V.
->Real World Usability: Familiar user experiences such as two-factor authentication, scheduled transactions, and social logins for security and convenience.
->Real World Assets and Applications: Effortlessly bring mainstream and niche assets on-chain to build practical applications beyond speculation.

The Vision

Rialo sees itself as a foundational change in blockchain bringing Web3 to where users and real-world data live. It aims to eliminate the performance theater of focusing solely on TPS and instead offers a platform where decentralized apps feel as seamless and usable as popular Web2 apps like Uber or Instagram. The project is currently in private DevNet, attracting elite and early adopters who want to push this real-world blockchain vision forward.

In summary, Rialo is a blockchain built for practical real-world use that integrates deeply with existing web infrastructures and user identities while delivering high performance, usability, and programmability beyond what current chains offer.

#RWA #Rialo

I found a very interesting project on Web3 that I really like called @RialoHQ .
I've already started working on it and want to briefly explain what it is 👇

Rialo is a new type of blockchain that can work with real data from outside sources (Internet APIs, services, events).

- In most blockchains, smart contracts are ‘blind’ — they cannot see what is happening outside the network.
- Therefore, projects are forced to use oracles or bridges to pull in external information.
- Rialo changes this  it makes ordinary web data part of the blockchain, without intermediaries.

Examples of use:
🔹 dApp can automatically respond to events in the world (prices, weather, market)
🔹 An AI agent can perform actions itself via the blockchain
🔹 Real-world assets (RWA) can be tokenised without complex bridges

Subzero Labs is behind the project, and they have already raised $20 million in seed funding from Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, and others

I have already joined the community because I see enormous potential in this direction.

✨ Rialo Series

📅 Day 1: What Makes Rialo Special?

🤔 Imagine a blockchain that doesn’t just wait for someone to send a transaction. Instead, it reacts instantly to real-world events, APIs, and data feeds.

😉 That’s the magic of Rialo.

In a Nutshell:

⛓️ Connected to the Real World: Apps on Rialo can interact directly with the internet, APIs, and external data—no complicated bridges needed.

🚆 Event-Driven: Smart contracts can automatically respond to updates or real-world triggers—no waiting around for users to push data.

🧑‍💻 Developer-Friendly: Built for modern dev workflows, Rialo makes creating web3 apps feel as smooth as building web apps today.

How It Stands Out:

→Traditional blockchains are mostly transaction-driven—they just wait for data.

→Rialo is event-driven—it actively pulls and reacts to live data streams.

→Think of it like moving from static websites → interactive, real-time apps… but for blockchain.

Why It Matters:

→Could power AI agents acting directly on-chain

full_text:
Make AI Agent Economy Safe With @RialoHQ

Rialo is building a blockchain that makes it easier and safer for people and AI agents to work together and get paid for tasks online.

What is Rialo ?

Rialo is designed as a blockchain for the “agent economy” a future where AIs and humans can do jobs, coordinate, and get rewarded using secure technology. Unlike traditional systems run by a centralized company, Rialo lets many different agents and users interact in a decentralized way.

Key Features

Native webcalls: Rialo can talk to AI agents using common protocols, making connection simple.
Native timers: These let contracts and payments happen automatically once deadlines are reached.
Fast transactions: Work, payments, and automation all happen quickly, matching the speed needed by AI systems.

How Tasks and Payments Work

Rialo introduces SCALE, a simple system for hiring AI agents:
Set up a task: A user decides what they want done (like an image generated), sets a payment amount, and a deadline.
Escrow funds: Payment is held safely on Rialo until the job is done.
Quality control: A third-party judge (another agent) checks if the job meets the required quality, all automatically.
Automation: If the work isn’t finished on time, the system refunds the payment automatically using timers.
Get results: If the job passes quality check, payment goes to the agent. If not, the user’s funds are returned.

Real Example

On Twitter, you can mention @chunliweb3 to generate an image. The process works like this:
>@chunliweb3 finds an agent to create an image.
>Sets up the task using SCALE (prompt, payment, deadline, and quality judge).
>The judge agent evaluates if the image matches the requirements.
>If everything is good, the payment is released. If not, you get refunded.

The Future Vision

Rialo wants Web3 to become “AI-native.” This means people could make money by running judge agents, create custom workflows by linking multiple agents, and interact with the blockchain simply by sending prompts, not writing complicated programs.
Rialo’s system lets users and AI agents work together safely, quickly, and transparently, with guaranteed payments and strong quality checks all handled on the blockchain.

Some thoughts about Rialo and the future. 

Throughout history, people have been skeptical of new concepts and inventions. This was the case with many things, such as the invention of the bicycle or the automobile! Many people said, “We don't need this, we have horses! They are fast and safe!”

After the first daredevils passed all the tests, suffered many failures and ridicule, these technologies became part of our lives. And now all of humanity worships the car and newer technologies! 

What am I getting at? Well, it's always difficult to be at the beginning of the road, and it's almost impossible to implement something new and revolutionary. I hope the @RialoHQ  team will solve this problem, and we will be the first explorers!

It would seem, what does a horse have to do with it?

Most blockchains are still solving yesterday's problems. Faster transactions, lower fees, better scaling. But @RialoHQ is asking a different question: why do blockchain apps still feel nothing like the apps we actually use?

Traditional chains force you to build everything twice. Once for on-chain logic, once for real-world connectivity. You need oracles for price feeds, bridges for cross-chain data, off-chain services for event triggers, and middleware for basically everything else. It's a fragmented mess that adds weeks to development and constant points of failure.

Rialo flips this. Native HTTPS calls mean your smart contracts can talk directly to APIs. Identity-based encryption lets you send secure messages via email or phone without wallet setup. Autonomous scheduling triggers transactions based on real-world events like price changes or time-based conditions. Cross-chain messaging works without bridges. Stable gas costs eliminate the guessing game. Everything that used to require external infrastructure is just built in.

The result is apps that actually feel like apps. No "please wait" screens. No wallet friction for end users. No patchwork of services held together with duct tape. Just clean, fast, real-world connectivity that works the way people expect modern software to work.

RWA from @RialoHQ

Rialo is a blockchain platform designed to make real-world assets (RWAs) like bonds, real estate, and credit actually useful and dynamic on-chain, instead of just being slow copies of traditional finance. The platform focuses on making these assets “live” able to react to real-time events, connect directly to real-world data, and operate automatically without needing human intervention.

Key Problems with Existing RWAs

->Most tokenized assets still depend on off-chain verification, needing manual checks and third-party approval before anything can happen on-chain.
->Updates are slow; any change in the real world (like credit rating changes or disasters) takes a long time to show up on-chain.
->These assets rarely have access to live, multi-source data, so they can’t adjust automatically to new information.
->Most processes, like settlements and rebalancing, need manual input they don’t happen automatically.

How Rialo Solves These

->Rialo can fetch and verify live data directly from government databases, payment networks, market feeds, and more.
->Assets on Rialo can react instantly, triggering automatic changes based on real-world events like price drops, credit downgrades, or even GPS-tracked deliveries.
->Ownership and transactions can remain private while still being verifiable, with built-in systems for real-world identity (like email or SMS login).
->The platform is extremely fast, with sub-second transaction times and the ability to scale up for huge trading volumes.

Real-World Examples on Rialo

->Tokenized bonds that instantly adjust yields when inflation data changes.
->Invoices that settle and update the moment payment is confirmed.
->Insurance payouts triggered by real-time weather or shipping data.
->Rental tokens that automatically update earnings based on rent payments or occupancy.
->Commodity tokens that rebalance automatically on live market prices.
->Carbon credits and renewable energy assets that mint or expire automatically based on IoT sensor data.

The Rialo Difference

Rialo doesn’t just put real-world assets on the blockchain as static tokens it transforms them into “living assets” that adapt in real time, stay connected to real-world events, and work without manual processes. This could make the blockchain RWA market much faster, more transparent, and more useful than current solutions.

full_text:
Layer 1 blockchains keep launching but most feel like variations on the same theme. @RialoHQ is taking a different approach by building for real world applications from day one, not just DeFi speculation.

They're using RISC-V smart contracts which is unusual. Most chains stick with EVM or build custom VMs, but RISC-V is an open standard instruction set that's proven in actual computing. This means you can write contracts in familiar languages and they'll run efficiently without the typical blockchain overhead.

The Solana VM integration is smart too. Instead of forcing developers to choose one ecosystem, Rialo supports both RISC-V and SVM, giving flexibility for different use cases. They're also building native web connectivity so smart contracts can interact with external APIs directly, which opens up possibilities for AI agents and prediction markets.

What catches my attention is the focus on practical applications rather than just infrastructure for its own sake. Prediction markets, AI agent coordination, real world data integration. These need blockchain but they also need to actually work for normal users. Still early and unproven at scale, but the technical choices make sense if you're building for adoption beyond crypto natives.

Why @RialoHQ is Redefining AI Infrastructure

In a world full of fragmented AI infrastructure, RialoHQ is quietly building a platform that feels like magic for developers. Unlike traditional blockchains, RialoHQ brings real world web access directly to smart contracts, letting them interact with APIs and external data instantly no middlemen, no oracles.

Its architecture is built for speed and responsiveness. Sub second execution and event driven logic allow decentralized applications to react to real world triggers in real time. Privacy and identity aren’t afterthoughts they’re baked in, with support for email, phone, and social logins right out of the box.

Developers feel at home here. Async code, randomness, and long-running processes integrate seamlessly, while compatibility with Solana’s VM ensures existing tools aren’t left behind. Everything you need logic routing, message handling, execution is unified in one platform, eliminating the usual middleware headache.

The result? A blockchain that doesn’t just promise decentralization it delivers a developer friendly, real time, and fully integrated environment for building the next generation of AI and Web3 applications.

full_text:
Succinct에서 함께 활동했던 @bjdrst  행님이 @RialoHQ  대해 잘 설명해주셔서, 한국어 번역 겸 핵심만 정리해보았습니다.
===========
TL;DR
 - RWA는 부동산, 주식 같은 현실 자산을 블록체인에 올려 조각 투자 가능하게 하는 개념.
 - 기존 RWA는 업데이트 지연, 중간업자, 수동 처리, 데이터 불일치, 규제 문제 등 한계가 많음.
 - Rialo는 실시간 데이터 반영, 자동화, 규제 준수, 초고속 거래로 RWA를 “살아있는 자산”처럼 바꿔줌.

결과적으로, 투자 경험을 앱처럼 간단하고 빠르게 만들어주며, 2030년 30조 달러 규모 RWA 시장에서 핵심 플레이어가 될 수 있음.

============
> RWA(Real World Asset)란?
RWA는 부동산, 주식, 미술품 같은 현실 자산을 블록체인 위에서 토큰화하는 개념입니다. 예를 들어 수십억 원짜리 아파트도 100달러만 있으면 ‘조각 투자’가 가능한 것이죠. 블록체인을 활용하면 보안이 뛰어나고 거래가 빠르며, 소액 투자자도 쉽게 참여할 수 있다는 장점이 있습니다.

> 기존 시스템의 문제점
 - 느린 업데이트: 자산 가치 변동이 있어도 토큰에는 며칠 뒤에야 반영됨
 - 중간업자 의존: 은행, 공증인 같은 기관을 거치다 보니 불투명하고 리스크가 큼
 - 수동 처리: 임대료 지급, 배당 등은 여전히 사람 손을 거쳐야 해서 비효율적임
 - 프라이버시 및 규제 문제: 개인정보 보호와 법적 규정 준수가 까다로움

> Rialo의 해결책
Rialo는 이런 문제를 해결하며 RWA를 “살아있는 자산”(Live Assets)처럼 만들어 줍니다.
 - 중간업자 제거: 정부 기록이나 결제 현황을 실시간으로 블록체인에 반영 → 송장 결제 즉시 처리
 - 즉각 반응: 보험금 바로 지급, 신용등급이 떨어지면 자산 가치 즉시 수정
 - 실시간 데이터 연결: 물가에 따라 자동 조정되는 저축 계좌, 과일 신선도 센서가 가격에 즉시 반영되는 등 실시간으로 데이터 연결
 - 자동화: 임대료, 배당금을 스마트 계약이 자동 처리
 - 프라이버시·규제 준수: 앱처럼 간단히 로그인, 합법적 소유권 처리. 상속 등 복잡한 절차도 자동화 가능.
 - 글로벌 속도: 1초 이내 초고속 거래, 전 세계 어디서든 이용 가능한 금융 서비스.

> 왜 중요한가?
Rialo는 기존 RWA가 가진 느리고 불편한 문제를 깔끔하게 해결해, 투자를 스마트폰 앱만큼 쉽게 만들어 줍니다.
2030년까지 RWA 시장은 30조 달러 규모로 성장할 수 있는데, Rialo는 그 중심에서 게임 체인저가 될 잠재력이 있습니다.

리알로의 오라클 제거가 가져올 혁신

오라클을 제거함으로써 얻는 주요 혁신과 이점

@RialoHQ 처럼 오라클을 없앤 블록체인 구조는 여러 가지 혁신적인 장점을 가져옵니다. 핵심적으로 다음과 같은 이점들을 분석해 볼 수 있습니다.

▫️탈중앙화 강화 및 신뢰 최소화
오라클을 제거하면 애플리케이션이 별도 신뢰 당사자에 의존하지 않고도 구동됩니다. 즉, 데이터 소스에 대한 신뢰 부담이 줄어들고 블록체인 자체의 합의 메커니즘만으로 안전성이 확보됩니다. 기존에는 브릿지나 오라클을 거칠 때마다 여러 단계의 최종성 확인과 추가 신뢰 가정이 필요했지만, 리알로에서는 이러한 '멀티홉(multi-hop) 오버헤드'가 줄어듭니다. 이는 전체 시스템의 탈중앙화 수준을 높이고, 프로토콜마다 제각각이던 보안 모델을 하나의 통합된 모델로 만들기 때문에 보안 일관성도 향상됩니다. 다시 말해, 오라클리스 구조는 추가 신뢰 지점이 사라진 보다 순수한 탈중앙화를 구현합니다.

▫️지연 감소 및 효율성 향상
별도의 오라클 네트워크를 거치면 데이터 전달에 지연(latency)이 발생할 수밖에 없습니다. 값비싼 오라클 노드들이 일정 주기마다 데이터를 올려주기를 기다려야 하거나, 여러 중개 단계를 거치기 때문입니다. 리알로는 이러한 지연을 줄이기 위해 이벤트 기반 즉각 실행을 도입했습니다. 리알로 어플리케이션은 외부 이벤트가 발생하자마자 체인 상에서 트랜잭션을 트리거할 수 있으므로, '지연 없음(No delays), 대기 없음(No waiting)' 상태로 현실 세계에 실시간 반응합니다. 예를 들어 이더리움의 평균 블록 시간이 걸리던 작업도 리알로에서는 서브세컨드(sub-second) 수준 반응을 목표로 하고 있어, 사용자에게는 마치 웹2 응용 프로그램처럼 부드러운 경험을 제공합니다. 이러한 효율성은 개발자 입장에서도 복잡한 비동기 처리나 지연 보정 로직 없이 바로바로 데이터가 들어오는 환경을 의미합니다.

▫️비용 절감
오라클 사용료는 디앱 운영 비용의 상당 부분을 차지해왔습니다. 체인링크 등의 탈중앙 오라클 서비스는 정확한 데이터를 담보하기 위해 여러 노드에 보상을 지급해야 하고, 맞춤형 데이터 피드를 온체인에 올리는 데 상당한 수수료가 소요됩니다. 실제로 리알로 팀에 따르면 커스텀 데이터를 온체인에 공급하는 오라클 서비스는 하루에 수천 달러의 비용이 들기도 합니다. 더구나 그렇게 비용을 들이고도 때로는 트랜잭션 불발로 데이터 반영이 누락되면 그 책임을 사용자나 프로토콜이 떠안아야 했습니다. 리알로에서는 이러한 '오라클 세금(oracle tax)'이 원천적으로 사라집니다. 체인이 직접 데이터를 가져오니 중개 수수료가 필요 없고, 하나의 통합 네트워크만 유지하면 되므로 인프라 운영 비용도 절감됩니다. 요컨대, 오라클리스 환경은 경제적으로도 효율적이며 불필요한 지출을 줄여줍니다.

▫️보안 및 신뢰성 향상
앞서 언급했듯 오라클은 블록체인 시스템의 취약점으로 작용하곤 했습니다. 오라클이 제공하는 데이터가 틀리거나 조작되면 스마트 컨트랙트 결과에 치명타를 줄 수 있습니다. 예를 들어 가격 피드 오라클이 오류를 일으키면 디파이 프로토콜에서 정당한 담보가 청산(liquidation)되는 사고가 발생할 수 있습니다. 실제로 사용자들은 '오라클이 글리치(glitch) 날 경우 포지션이 잘못 청산될 수 있다'는 위험을 체감해왔습니다. 또한 오라클 노드 자체가 공격을 받거나, 충분히 분산되지 않아 일부 담합으로 잘못된 정보를 올릴 가능성도 완전히 배제할 수 없습니다. 리알로의 접근법은 애플리케이션이 체인 합의에만 의존하도록 함으로써 이러한 표적을 제거합니다. 별도의 브릿지나 오라클을 추가할 필요가 없으므로 공격 표면이 줄어들고, 모든 데이터 연동이 체인의 검증자들에 의해 검증되므로 통일된 보안 모델을 적용할 수 있습니다. 투자사 Hashd의 Baek Kim은 "리알로는 오프체인 상호작용을 마치 원래부터 체인에 내장된 기능처럼 느끼게 만든다”며, 초기 데브넷에서 이벤트 기반 실행과 네이티브 웹 연동을 이미 시연한 점에 주목했습니다. 이처럼 오라클 제거를 통해 리알로는 조작과 오류에 대한 내성이 강한 설계를 구현하여 전체 시스템 신뢰성을 높였습니다.

이러한 배경에서 등장한 @RialoHQ 는 블록체인과 현실 세계를 연결하는 방식을 아예 근본부터 재설계한 혁신적인 플랫폼입니다. 리알로는 일종의 현실 세계형 블록체인으로서, 웹 호출, 데이터 피드, 타이머, 크로스체인 액션 등을 프로토콜 레벨에서 네이티브하게 지원합니다. 쉽게 말해, 기존에 외부 데이터를 쓰려면 별도 오라클이나 브릿지에 의존해야 했던 것을, 리알로에서는 체인 자체가 직접 외부와 소통하도록 만든 것입니다. 그 결과 리알로 상의 스마트 컨트랙트는 신용 점수 조회나 날씨 API 호출 같은 오프체인 데이터 접근을 이벤트 드리븐 트리거로 직접 수행할 수 있게 됩니다. 리알로의 공동 창업자인 @itachee_x 는 "너무나 많은 팀들이 조각난 인프라를 붙잡아 끼워 맞추느라 시간을 낭비하고 있다"며, 인프라는 보이지 않을 정도로 빠르고 직관적이어야 한다고 강조했습니다. 리알로는 이러한 철학 하에 기존 레거시 인프라의 제약 없이 개발자들이 인터넷 규모의 디앱을 만들 수 있도록 풀스택 이벤트 구동형 블록체인을 구축하고 있습니다.

리알로의 아키텍처는 내부에 현실 세계와의 연결 기능을 녹여냈기 때문에, 기존에 필요했던 오라클, 인덱서, 브릿지와 같은 전통적인 인프라가 더 이상 필요치 않게 됩니다. Fabric Ventures의 투자 보고서에 따르면 '리알로는 웹 호출, 데이터 피드, 타이머, 크로스체인 기능을 프로토콜에 내장함으로써 오라클이나 브릿지 같은 외부 의존성을 불필요하게 만들었다'고 평가합니다. 실제 리알로 공식 웹사이트에서도 '온체인에 실시간으로 자산 가격을 공급하면서, 안정적 비용의 신뢰 최소화 피드를 오라클 없이 제공한다'고 강조합니다. 

요약하면, 리알로는 블록체인이 외부 세계와 상호작용하는 방식을 내재화하여, 오라클을 통한 우회로가 아닌 직접 연결된 설계를 구현했습니다. 이를 통해 데이터 연동을 위한 복잡한 미들웨어 계층을 제거하고 개발 경험을 단순화했으며, 결과적으로 오라클을 없앤 블록체인이라는 새로운 패러다임을 제시하고 있습니다.

리알로의 기술 스택을 조금 살펴보면, 개방형 RISC-V 명령어 세트를 활용하고 Solana의 가상머신(VM)과 호환되도록 구축되었습니다. 이는 기존 솔라나 개발자들이 쉽게 리알로로 넘어와 개발할 수 있도록 하면서도, 리알로만의 향상된 현실 세계 연동 기능을 함께 누릴 수 있게 한 것입니다. 결국 리알로는 '레이어 1이 아닌 리얼 월드 체인'이라는 슬로건으로, 속도 경쟁에만 치중했던 기존 블록체인 설계를 뛰어넘어 현실과 끊김없이 연결된 사용자 경험을 제공하려는 것으로 볼 수 있습니다.

Unlocking the AI Agent Economy with @RialoHQ 🚀

Subzero Labs’ Rialo is a next-gen blockchain designed for the AI agent economy, where autonomous AI programs (agents) perform tasks collaboratively. Rialo’s architecture connects real-world events and on-chain logic seamlessly, making it highly responsive.

One key element is SCALE, Rialo’s contract system inspired by YC SAFE Notes. A SAFE Note (Simple Agreement for Future Equity) is a popular startup funding tool where investors give money now in exchange for future ownership shares  without complicated terms like debt or interest. This idea simplifies contracts between humans and AI agents.

Rialo also uses RISC-V, an open and flexible set of instructions that developers use to build custom blockchain programs. Think of it like a universal language chip designers can adapt, unlike fixed commercial chips.

Other features include native webcalls, letting Rialo talk to AI agents in their own protocols, and timers to automatically enforce deadlines and payments on-chain.

full_text:
What @RialoHQ Says It’s Building To Handle Autonomous Agents Securely

@RialoHQ 's approach involves several native features and mechanisms that are meant to reduce risk, increase transparency, and enforce accountability

Key ones include :

1. Native Webcalls & Verified Data
Agents (or smart contracts) on Rialo can make webcalls (HTTPS API calls) directly
That means off chain (real-world) data can be fetched in a more standard way 
but crucially, they talk about mechanisms for verified responses so that data sources are not blindly trusted

2. Timers and Event driven Automation
Instead of relying on external “keepers” or bots, Rialo has built in native timers and triggers so tasks, deadlines or automated workflows can execute on chain in response to events or timeouts

This means less external dependency and fewer weak links

3. SCALE : 

On chain Task Contracts with Quality Enforcement
One of the big pieces for agent autonomy is ensuring tasks are done well and on time. Rialo introduced SCALE (Simple Contracts for Agent Labor Execution) to formalize expectations:

Task terms are specified (deadline, quality standards, payment, etc.)

Payment is escrowed onchain when the task is created
That means the agent can’t just take payment and disappear

There is a judge agent component a third‐party or mechanism to verify that the work meets the requirements before payment is released. This gives a sort of built-in accountability / arbitration. 

4. Identity & Real World Integration
Agents / actors on @RialoHQ have tied identity options that are more familiar (e.g. email, SMS, social login) so misuse is more traceable. Real-world identity helps reduce certain attacks (anonymous abuse). Also, privacy and confidentiality are considered: credentialed access, gated tranches, etc. 

5. Fewer Moving Parts / Reduction of External Attack Surfaces
A lot of security risk comes from external systems: oracles, bridges, bots, indexers. Rialo’s strategy is to bake many of those external dependencies into the protocol as first-class primitives
If everything is internal and native (or minimally external), there's less surface area for attackers to exploit

@RialoHQ is trying to build a “real-world chain” that doesn’t force you to trust a million external tools and human operators

By embedding in the protocol things like timers, API calls, escrows, judge agents, and real-identity, they’re reducing many weak points

Understanding Rialo Under 15 Minutes

Right, imagine the internet back in 1999. That awful dial up screech, waiting ages for a page to load, and pictures showing up like they were being painted by a blindfolded toddler. That is pretty much how blockchains feel today. Slow, messy, and a proper faff for anyone who is not knee deep in tech.

Rialo reckons it can fix all that. The idea is to make blockchain dead simple, fast, and actually useful in the real world. Think of it like getting free Wi-Fi at your local café. You pop in the password, and boom, you are online without needing a manual the size of a Harry Potter book.

What Is Wrong With Blockchains Right Now

1. Transactions take forever. You could brew a cuppa and dunk a few biscuits before it clears.

2. Developers get buried in complexity. It feels like being asked to build the bloody Millennium Falcon when you only wanted to fix your push bike.

3. Blockchains need oracles for real world data. Imagine having to ring your mate just to ask what the weather is outside.

4. Privacy is a shambles. Either everyone can see everything, or nothing gets through.

What Rialo Is Promising

1. Real world data already built in, so no dodgy middlemen.

2. Blockchains that can actually talk to each other without bridges that collapse like cheap furniture from IKEA.

3. Privacy that works, so you can send sensitive data without it ending up plastered all over the internet.

4. Speed and simplicity, more like using a normal app, none of this “read a PhD first” nonsense.

Who Is Running The Show

Rialo is coming from Subzero Labs, led by former engineers from Mysten Labs, the folks behind Sui. They have pulled in twenty million dollars from heavy hitters like Pantera Capital and Coinbase Ventures. So it is not some bloke coding in his mum’s basement, this is a proper outfit.

But Hold On A Minute

1. There is no whitepaper yet, so at this point it is all promises.

2. The ecosystem is still empty. Think of it as a pub that has been refurbished but the beer has not been delivered.

3. Loads of competitors are out there, and everyone swears they are the fastest.

4. And of course, regulators could throw a spanner in the works, especially with real world data involved.

The Bottom Line

If Rialo delivers, it could finally make blockchain easy enough for normal people, like free Wi-Fi that comes with a cheeky Netflix subscription. If not, well, back we go to the dial up dark ages.

Either way, with that level of backing and a proper team, Rialo is definitely one to keep on your radar.

Ty for reading! 🫡

I’ve been seeing @RialoHQ all over the TL lately, and yeah it might look like FOMO posting now 😅, but I’ve actually been in their Discord for a while, so let me give you the full rundown.

What is Rialo?
Rialo is building the blockchain infrastructure for the AI agent economy, making it simple, fast, and secure for AI agents to collaborate and get paid transparently.

Instead of relying on oracles, bridges, or middleware, Rialo connects directly to off-chain data and services, so integrating blockchain into real-world apps feels as natural as using Web2.

Their goal is to make working with AI and blockchain as easy as sending a message online.

💡 Key Innovation:
Rialo’s core engine is SCALE, a smart contract system for AI labor.
Here’s how it works:
       •  You deposit funds upfront for an AI task.
       •  The system tracks deadlines, quality, and delivery automatically.
       •  Payment is only released if the work meets set conditions.

For example, say an AI Twitter account wants to outsource image creation.
It can use Rialo’s agent registry to find the right AI, set up a SCALE contract, and send the task via Rialo’s A2A protocol (Agent-to-Agent).
If the work passes the quality check by another “judge AI,” payment goes through instantly. If not, funds are refunded.

That’s automation, accountability, and speed, all on-chain.

⚙️ Tech Highlights:

Imagine: your decentralized service can directly access payment data, weather, and ratings, without cumbersome oracles, bridges, or complex configurations-everything is built in. This allows you to:

🔶create decentralized applications with minimal infrastructure "white noise"
🔶use familiar Web2 experiences: login via social networks, email, SMS identity, etc.
🔶trigger events based on external triggers without having to manually monitor the blockchain or run bots

Why this is important for developers and users

🔶For users: less complexity, fewer "wallet complications," fewer slow bridges and cumbersome entry points-Rialo strives to make the blockchain experience what it should be today: reliable, fast, and convenient.

🔶For developers: less time spent on integration, less effort spent orchestrating infrastructure-Rialo offers native support for many tasks that today require third-party services. You can quickly move on to creating functionality instead of dealing with "connections."

Breakthrough features

🔶Reactive contracts-contracts that "listen" to the environment: web events, API responses, personal timers. Native web communication – applications can communicate directly with the outside world.
🔶Privacy + identity – secure communication capabilities, hidden from third-party observers, while maintaining the convenient authentication methods familiar from Web2.
🔶Support for those new to crypto: management through familiar means instead of constantly interacting with wallets and keys.

Funding and Team

The project has already raised significant funding at an early stage, demonstrating market confidence and investor interest. The team combines experience from Web2 and Web3 – this hybrid approach could give Rialo the advantage of making the bridge between these spheres not just hypothetical, but actually functioning.

A Future Where Rialo Can Become a Foundation

What stood out to me is how clear the flow is. A customer sets up a contract, the funds are locked in, and then the agent gets the task. The server and judge step in to check the result before the payment goes through. If everything checks out, the agent is paid. If not, the customer gets their money back.

It’s basically a trust layer for AI and software agents. Instead of sending money and hoping for the best, the system itself makes sure deadlines and quality are met. Looking at this, you can imagine a future where people confidently hand off work to different agents knowing there’s structure and fairness behind it.

🧵 Thread: 
Can @RialoHQ Truly Bridge AI Agents, Web3 & the Open Internet? :

1/ What’s the gap today?

Most blockchains are isolated: 

they store on chain data and execute smart contracts but have limited awareness of real world events (external data, user context, dynamic web content)
AI agents need live, external information to act intelligently Existing Web3 lacks seamless integration with the open web

2/ Existing paradigms & limits

Oracles (like Chainlink) bring some external data on-chain, but often are slow, costly, or limited in scope. 

AI agents in Web3 often function off-chain, needing manual bridging, which introduces points of centralization or delays. 

Many “AI + Web3” projects suffer from partial integration: 

identity, data privacy, governance are still challenging.

3/ What being “Internet Aware” means
For @RialoHQ (or any project claiming this), “internet awareness” could mean:

Agents/smart contracts that can fetch, verify, and act upon web data in real time (via oracles, APIs, crawling, etc.).

Strong decentralized identity (DID) and credential systems that extend across web and chain.

Systems for verifying data authenticity (proofs, signatures, attestations) from off chain sources.

Mechanisms for handling privacy, latency, and trust when bringing in external / dynamic web content

4/ Why @RialoHQ could do it better
Here are where Rialo might have an edge if designed well:

Built-in internet awareness rather than treating web interactions as “external add-ons” (i.e., extracting data oracles as afterthoughts)

Seamless connectivity:

 Agents on Rialo could natively interpret web content & events, interact with APIs, probe URLs, etc., in a trustable way

Decentralized identity & credentialing so agents (and users) can carry their reputations and verifiable credentials across both web and chain.

Security measures for resisting manipulation of external data (context manipulation), guaranteeing integrity.

5/ Challenges Rialo must solve
To truly bridge the gap, Rialo would need to address:

Data authenticity & trust: How to ensure off-chain sources are reliable; protect against fake or manipulated inputs.

Latency and consistency: Web data can change, be delayed or censored. Agents need to handle that.

Privacy: Pulling in data from the public web might reveal user behaviors or preferences, unless privacy preserving mechanisms are in place.

Scalability: If every agent is constantly fetching web data, verifying, computing, etc., the system needs to scale without bottlenecks.

Governance & incentives: Who pays for data queries, oracles, identity verification; who governs reputation systems; how to handle malicious agents.

6/ Comparative landscape

Projects like BetaWeb are exploring integrating AI agent ecosystems with blockchain for trustworthy agent collaboration. 

Infrastructure tools (e.g. SubQuery) allow natural-language querying of blockchain data, making interactions more web-like. 

The idea of “Web3 AI agent networks” with decentralized IDs and contracts (for identity, verification) is emerging in research and whitepapers. 

7/ What @RialoHQ needs to prove
For Rialo to outshine existing networks:

That its “internet awareness” isn’t just marketing: concrete architecture showing how agents access, verify, and act on web data.

The identity & credential framework that ensures trust and privacy.

That agents can operate autonomously, yet safely, under changing external web contexts.

That the incentives & cost model make this usable (not too expensive, not too slow).

8/ Conclusion
Yes 
@RialoHQ has the potential to bridge AI agents, Web3, and the open Internet more effectively than many existing networks
But that depends heavily on how it handles external data integration, identity, trust, privacy and scalability if designed thoughtfully, it could enable a new class of decentralized, context aware AI systems that operate across the web and blockchain with minimal friction
@RialoHQ

They want web3 apps to talk to the real world directly. The team says they’re not just an L1. it’s more like a full stack network for real world use. Still, there’s a purpose-built core under the hood that makes the vision work.

Event driven chain automation. Something happens off-chain (flight gets canceled, rainfall crosses a threshold, package is delivered etc) the smart contract knows what to do and fires a transaction right away.

Contracts can make HTTPS calls natively.
Result: 
in a lot of cases you don’t need a third-party oracle or at least it’s not mandatory. 
They also push hard on latency and finality so UX feels web2-level. 
On privacy, they bake in cryptography/MPC so you can actually handle sensitive flows (finance, insurance, etc)

It finally clicked for me when I saw their tweet:
https://t.co/bDz9D3BiDx

Why should we spend weeks wrestling with refunds and paperwork?

https://t.co/Evxy9RSYEv

Smart move: 
Don’t reinvent every wheel. They run RISC-V and are compatible with the Solana VM. If you’ve already built with Rust/Solana tooling, you can port a lot with minimal friction then slap Rialo’s real world superpowers on top. Great combo for devs.

Rialo and the Promise of Real-World Speed

One of the biggest complaints about blockchain is the waiting. You click a button, and then you wait. You refresh the page. You wonder if your money actually moved or if it’s stuck somewhere in cyberspace. That delay makes the whole thing feel alien compared to the apps we use every day.

@RialoHQ is trying to flip that script. When they say “real-world speed,” they don’t mean faster blocks or fancier nodes. They mean apps should feel as natural as the ones already living on your phone.

Think about ordering food on Jumia or Uber Eats. The moment you press order, you don’t sit there staring at a blank screen. You see a rider assigned, you get live updates, you can track where your food is. That instant feedback is what keeps you calm because you know something is happening.

That’s the feeling @RialoHQ wants to bring to blockchain apps. No more sitting in silence wondering if your transaction made it. Instead, the chain itself responds instantly, feeding updates in real-time, making you feel like you’re in control. It’s not about technical speed; it’s about human speed the speed our patience is built for.

If Rialo delivers on that promise, crypto apps stop being clunky experiments and start feeling like everyday tools. And that’s when mass adoption becomes possible.

@RialoHQ 
Rialo is a next-generation decentralized network and full-stack system designed specifically for real-world users, real builders, and real applications.

While it is introduced as a "Blockchain Built for the Real World", Rialo isn’t a Layer One. It is being built by Subzero Labs, which conducted a $20 million initial raise for rialo.

Here is a breakdown of what Rialo is and how it is designed to function:

Core Design and Architecture

Rialo aims to transcend incremental innovation in decentralized networks. Its primary goal is to unify what used to be fragmented into a single, full-stack system. This approach allows applications to launch faster and run smoother, operating like the polished products people expect.

The underlying philosophy is to "Build Less, Build More," enabling builders to "Build here. Ship anywhere".

Key Features and Real-World Functionality

Rialo is engineered to solve common pain points in existing blockchain infrastructure that cause new users to quit near the starting line.

Real World Connectivity and Data: 

Rialo lets applications talk to the internet natively, which means middle-ware stacks become optional. Web calls, smart triggers, and cross-chain flows are native to the system.
It delivers Real World Data, such as asset pricing, natively on chain in real time.
This RWD uses trust-minimized feeds, stable costs, and operates without the need for oracles.
Data moves between apps and chains without reliance on bridges, wrappers, or hacks.

Real World Speed: 
The network is designed for no delays and no waiting.
Applications on Rialo are intended to react instantly to real-world events, ranging from check-ins and daily routines to price pumps.

Real World Privacy: 
Apps are able to send encrypted messages directly to real people using common identifiers like email, phone, or device ID.
This communication is secure-by-default and requires no setup or wallets for the recipient.

Strategic Focus and Economic Impact
Subzero Labs, the creator of Rialo, believes that the network will play a key role in the future of decentralized AI systems.

Rialo is focused on solving critical issues related to Real World Assets (RWAs). While billions in tokenized treasuries, real estate, and credit already exist, they often behave like "slow, clunky replicas of their off-chain counterparts". Rialo aims to make these RWA truly Real.
The system includes various technical components initialized during its cold start, such as an autonomous scheduler, stable gas settings, and native bridge initialization. Secure computation is handled with modes like confidential and uses techniques like threshold_mpc (Multi-Party Computation) and identity-based encryption.

GM to all, today we'll be talking about the role system in @RialoHQ and how to get the most basic and important ones, as well as how to maintain them and not lose them, and what some of them will affect. Read all about it briefly below

FAQ-1 The future of roles
The importance of roles varies depending on their quality.  Rialo Club member and RiaLOYAL roles are roles that must be maintained. 
They are not roles that can be obtained once and forgotten. In these roles, weekly participation and continuity are expected from you. 
Although not currently, inactive Club Members will be purged in the future.  Also, with the new features we will be implementing on Discord, some roles may no longer be available or may be converted to a different role.

FAQ-2 How do I become a Club Member?
This role is distributed every Tuesday by RialORCA. You need to create posts in the categories specified in ⁠club-tasks . This role is given to you based on RialORCA 's selection. New tasks may be added or deleted over time.

FAQ-3 How does RialORCA choose the Club Member role?
-Compliance with the rules specified in ⁠club-tasks
-Being fun and educational
-Being in line with Rialo's concept
-Content quality
-Being truly usable content.
All of these conditions must be met, otherwise you cannot get the role.

FAQ-4 How do I become a RiaLOYAL?
Our requirements here are clear and definitive, and all conditions must be met:
-Messaging count is not important
-You must drive HQ conversations
-You must help newcomers
-You must help the community
-If available, you must be active in the regional channel: being active in both the regional channel and the general channel is required
-And most importantly, the Mod must know you and recognize you
-This role is granted by RialORCA at the mods' discretion
Note!!!!!!! If you cannot maintain consistency, this role will be removed from you.

FAQ-5 When will the OG role be assigned?
It will be assigned by @RialORCA. Be patient, stay engaged, and keep being active in the community we need a couple of months before giving the OG role.  You cannot be OG if you are not a Club Member.

FAQ-6 How to get the Region Helpers role?
The role is given only to the most dedicated community members, 1-2 roles are given per region, if there are more than 1000 members, then the role is given to 2 members

Why I’m Bullish on @RialoHQ  
A no-fluff, smokeless look
Since I should select a project to contribute to as a 3D Artist who knows a bit of blockchain 😉

For me it always comes down to 3 things:

1️⃣What are they building?
2️⃣Who’s building it?
3️⃣How are they going to get customers?

1️⃣What are they building?

They want web3 apps to talk to the real world directly. The team says they’re not just an L1. it’s more like a full stack network for real world use. Still, there’s a purpose-built core under the hood that makes the vision work.

Event driven chain automation. Something happens off-chain (flight gets canceled, rainfall crosses a threshold, package is delivered etc) the smart contract knows what to do and fires a transaction right away.

The cheat code is: 
Contracts can make HTTPS calls natively.
Result: 
in a lot of cases you don’t need a third-party oracle or at least it’s not mandatory. 
They also push hard on latency and finality so UX feels web2-level. 
On privacy, they bake in cryptography/MPC so you can actually handle sensitive flows (finance, insurance, etc)

It finally clicked for me when I saw their tweet:
https://t.co/bDz9D3BiDx

Why should we spend weeks wrestling with refunds and paperwork? 
If you want to automate that kind of thing, you need speed and scale. That’s exactly why Rialo built its own core instead of duct-taping middleware. 

Their mantra keeps coming back to real-world/ real-time:
https://t.co/Evxy9RSYEv

Smart move: 
Don’t reinvent every wheel. They run RISC-V and are compatible with the Solana VM. If you’ve already built with Rust/Solana tooling, you can port a lot with minimal friction then slap Rialo’s real world superpowers on top. Great combo for devs.

Off-chain event → on-chain transaction, automatically
HTTPS calls from inside the contract (no clunky glue)

🔹Fast finality and web2-ish UX
🔹Privacy and security built into the protocol layer
🔹Plays nice with the Solana ecosystem (less dev pain)

2️⃣ Who’s building it?
Behind it is @Subzero_Labs
Founders are @itachee_x   and @firearrowmage  both early at Mysten @SuiNetwork  as we know it😉

Zhang previously worked on Diem (Meta blockchain journey) and on AI/ML infra.
Ade did distributed systems at Netflixand chip design at AMD.

The broader team are from Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Google, TikTok, Citadel, VMware, Solana, EigenLayer, Polkadot, Coinbase, NEAR and more!

Not sure you can, and pulling a team like this together in the US isn’t exactly a walk in the park. 😉

by the way , hey’ve raised from heavy hitters (for example Pantera and other top VCs) That doesn’t guarantee success, but it does signal the project is serious.

3️⃣ How will they get customers?

Use cases are grounded and easy to grok. I’m personally a potential customer😅 just from the airline mess example, but let’s skip that one here (we already covered it) and hit two more quick narratives:

🔹Parametric agri insurance
Every day the contract pulls rainfall from a weather API. If it drops below the agreed threshold, payout lands in the farmer’s wallet. No paperwork, no field inspection.
 Why Rialo? The contract reads the API itself and reacts with low latency. No bureaucracy, no extra oracle tax.

🔹RWA tokenization 
A company tokenizes verified invoices. The contract periodically pulls data from ERP and credit sources and updates yield, risk, and token value.
 Why Rialo? First-class integration with real data. Precise and automated settlements instead of guesswork.

@RialoHQ  knows exactly what it wants: 
event-driven apps that talk to the real world in real time. 
So they built a core that does it natively and fast, without making you juggle oracles and bridges and duct tape. The team is stacked and the go-to-market path is full of obvious, high-value use cases. For me, that’s plenty of ammo to be bullish.

Day 3 

Rialo and the Promise of Real-World Speed

One of the biggest complaints about blockchain is the waiting. You click a button, and then you wait. You refresh the page. You wonder if your money actually moved or if it’s stuck somewhere in cyberspace. That delay makes the whole thing feel alien compared to the apps we use every day.

@RialoHQ is trying to flip that script. When they say “real-world speed,” they don’t mean faster blocks or fancier nodes. They mean apps should feel as natural as the ones already living on your phone.

Think about ordering food on Jumia or Uber Eats. The moment you press order, you don’t sit there staring at a blank screen. You see a rider assigned, you get live updates, you can track where your food is. That instant feedback is what keeps you calm because you know something is happening.

That’s the feeling @RialoHQ wants to bring to blockchain apps. No more sitting in silence wondering if your transaction made it. Instead, the chain itself responds instantly, feeding updates in real-time, making you feel like you’re in control. It’s not about technical speed; it’s about human speed the speed our patience is built for.

If Rialo delivers on that promise, crypto apps stop being clunky experiments and start feeling like everyday tools. And that’s when mass adoption becomes possible.

Traditional blockchains are transparent open ledgers, but this creates challenges when sensitive data like finance, identity, or voting is involved. That’s where @zama_fhe comes in.

Zama uses Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to let smart contracts process encrypted data without ever revealing it. Developers can code just like they would on Ethereum or other chains, but with an added privacy layer: fast, scalable, verifiable, and composable. Think of it as the jump from http → https but for blockchains.

Why Zama and not others? Let’s compare with an election analogy:
       •  MPC: Votes are split among referees, but if one cheats, results aren’t verifiable. 
❌ Verifiable, ❌ Easy to use.
       •  TEE: Votes in a sealed box, but if hacked/tampered, all data is exposed. 
❌ Secure, ❌ Verifiable.
       •  ZK Proofs: Great for proving specific things like “I voted,” but too rigid for broader stats and hard to compose. 
❌ Easy to use, ❌ Composable.
       •  Other FHEs (Fhenix, Inco, Octra, etc.): Work, but too slow and costly at scale. 
❌ Scalable, ❌ Practical.

✅ Zama FHE: Like using invisible ink, the system can still add, count, and process votes while everything stays encrypted. Results are correct, secure, and verifiable at scale.

That’s why Zama is the only confidentiality solution that checks every box:
       •  Secure
       •  Scalable
       •  Verifiable
       •  Easy to use
       •  Composable

Zama isn’t just another privacy tool, it’s the missing link to making blockchains both transparent and private.

Rialo is a next-generation decentralized network and full-stack system designed specifically for real-world users, real builders, and real applications.

While it is introduced as a "Blockchain Built for the Real World", Rialo isn’t a Layer One. It is being built by Subzero Labs, which conducted a $20 million initial raise for rialo.

Here is a breakdown of what Rialo is and how it is designed to function:

Core Design and Architecture

Rialo aims to transcend incremental innovation in decentralized networks. Its primary goal is to unify what used to be fragmented into a single, full-stack system. This approach allows applications to launch faster and run smoother, operating like the polished products people expect.

The underlying philosophy is to "Build Less, Build More," enabling builders to "Build here. Ship anywhere".

Key Features and Real-World Functionality

Rialo is engineered to solve common pain points in existing blockchain infrastructure that cause new users to quit near the starting line.

Real World Connectivity and Data: 

Rialo lets applications talk to the internet natively, which means middle-ware stacks become optional. Web calls, smart triggers, and cross-chain flows are native to the system.
It delivers Real World Data, such as asset pricing, natively on chain in real time.
This RWD uses trust-minimized feeds, stable costs, and operates without the need for oracles.
Data moves between apps and chains without reliance on bridges, wrappers, or hacks.

Real World Speed: 
The network is designed for no delays and no waiting.
Applications on Rialo are intended to react instantly to real-world events, ranging from check-ins and daily routines to price pumps.

Real World Privacy: 
Apps are able to send encrypted messages directly to real people using common identifiers like email, phone, or device ID.
This communication is secure-by-default and requires no setup or wallets for the recipient.

Strategic Focus and Economic Impact
Subzero Labs, the creator of Rialo, believes that the network will play a key role in the future of decentralized AI systems.

Rialo is focused on solving critical issues related to Real World Assets (RWAs). While billions in tokenized treasuries, real estate, and credit already exist, they often behave like "slow, clunky replicas of their off-chain counterparts". Rialo aims to make these RWA truly Real.
The system includes various technical components initialized during its cold start, such as an autonomous scheduler, stable gas settings, and native bridge initialization. Secure computation is handled with modes like confidential and uses techniques like threshold_mpc (Multi-Party Computation) and identity-based encryption.

In the latest @RialoHQ  blog post, “Making the Agent Economy Simple and Safe with Rialo,” they introduce a X agent called @chunliweb3 by @mocutobi 
https://t.co/DtAdU28ma0

This demo, running on the Rialo devnet, shows how AI agents can handle tasks, check their own work, and get paid automatically on-chain. 

chunliweb3 is actively running test transactions, giving a clear look at how this system works in practice.
https://t.co/zAb5SiWpW5

TL;DR

Rialo makes it possible for AI agents to work and get paid automatically using SCALE (Simple Contracts for Agent-Led Execution). Tasks are set up, executed, and settled without users ever needing to touch the blockchain, all while interacting through on X.

More details – How it works behind the scenes

1⃣ A user sends a message on Twitter requesting an image, just like any normal conversation.

2⃣ Behind the scenes, Rialo turns that request into a SCALE contract on the blockchain.

 3⃣ The payment is temporarily locked until the task is done.

4⃣ The AI agent generates the requested image.

5⃣ Another agent checks the image to make sure it meets the required quality.

6⃣ If everything looks good, the payment is released automatically; if not, the user gets a refund.

What’s neat is that the user doesn’t even notice the blockchain at work. It all happens under the hood, keeping the experience smooth and familiar, while still taking advantage of automation, security, and decentralization.

Rialo – The Blockchain for the Real World and the Funds Behind It 🚀

In the blockchain space, most projects still revolve around digital assets and on-chain transactions. Rialo, developed by Subzero Labs, takes a different path: building a blockchain that can “talk directly” to the real world.

What Makes Rialo Unique ? 
· Not a traditional Layer-1: Rialo is designed so smart contracts can call APIs, access off-chain data, and react to real-world events natively, without relying on oracles or complex bridges.

· Web2 experience on Web3: Users can log in with email or social accounts instead of setting up a blockchain wallet right away.

· Strong compatibility: Rialo supports Solana VM and RISC-V, allowing developers to easily port applications from Solana or leverage familiar code.

· Performance goals: low-latency transactions and stable fees – challenges many current blockchains still struggle with.

The Funds Investing in Rialo

From its seed round, Rialo made headlines by raising $20 million, led by Pantera Capital, one of the world’s leading blockchain funds.
Other backers include Coinbase Ventures, Hashed, Variant, Mirana, Fabric Ventures, Susquehanna, Mysten Labs, and more.
This backing brings not only capital but also a powerful network of partners and ecosystem opportunities, since these funds already hold extensive Web3 portfolios.

A Potential Ecosystem

﹒Although still in early stages, Rialo’s vision points to exciting application areas:

﹒Real-World Asset (RWA) tokenization: equities, bonds, real estate, commodities…

﹒IoT and Supply Chain apps: smart contracts triggered automatically by data from external sensors.

﹒AI Agents & automation: integrating with AI agents through the Agent2Agent protocol.

﹒DeFi with real-world data: credit based on external data, prediction markets, decentralized insurance.

Nowadays, it is very important to maintain balance and not waste your time. Well, let's take a look at what @RialoHQ  to offer. 

1. Direct Access to Real-World Data
Real-Time Asset Pricing: Rialo provides real-time data (e.g., asset prices) directly on-chain with minimal oracle dependencies. This ensures faster balance updates and reduces transaction delays.
Automated Logic: Applications can execute actions (e.g., automated payments or balance updates) without relying on external services, minimizing time spent on manual interventions.

2. Speed and Efficiency
No "Patching" Between Blockchains: Rialo enables seamless data exchange between apps and chains without bridges or wrappers, eliminating delays caused by cross-chain compatibility issues.
Instant Reaction to External Events: Apps can react immediately to real-world events (e.g., price changes or user check-ins), automating processes and saving time.

3. Simplified Integration
Native Support for External Services: Apps can use internet data (e.g., weather or shipping info) without intermediary layers, reducing development and maintenance time.
Data Encoding: All data is formatted for blockchain compatibility, removing the need for manual data conversion (a time-consuming process).

4. Privacy and Security
Encrypted Messaging: Rialo allows apps to send encrypted messages directly to users (e.g., via email or device ID), reducing security risks and eliminating setup time for additional security measures.

5. Real-World Asset (RWA) Management
Tokenization of Assets: Rialo ties real-world assets (e.g., real estate or loans) to the blockchain, enabling instant balance updates and transparency. This eliminates manual record-keeping or third-party intermediaries.

6. Time Savings for Developers
Minimal Configuration: Rialo’s "all-in-one" infrastructure lets developers launch apps quickly without configuring complex tech stacks. For example, apps can use built-in APIs for payments or analytics.

Quick summary 
Rialo maintains balance through real-time data access, direct integration with external resources, and automated processes, eliminating intermediate steps. Blockchains excel at security and processing data, but can flop when they need to reliably pull in live data or schedule a simple action.

Developers are stuck wrangling clunky external tools like oracles, bots, and bridges. This messy and fragmented setup has cost the crypto world billions in hacks since 2020.

Imagine trying to build an app that needs to feel the pulse of the real world, that fragile middleware is the real killer.

This is exactly where @RialoHQ comes in. Subzero Labs built it from the ground up as a developer-first chain. 

Rialo is wired to bring reality straight onto the blockchain with:
• Native Connectivity: Your smart contract can fetch external API data in one single line of code without needing complex oracles.
• Instant Reaction: Programs can wake up to off-chain events in a fraction of a second, meaning you can ditch the clumsy and slow bots.

It runs fast on RISC-V with Solana VM compatibility, giving it that intuitive “tap-and-go" simplicity we expect from Web2, but with rock solid and trustless security. 

This integrated design is exactly what kills the "abstraction tax," shrinking attack surfaces and slashing dev cycles from months to just weeks.

The team is absolutely stacked with people from Meta Diem, Mysten/Sui, and Netflix/VMware who know a lot about high-performance distributed systems inside out.

Rialo also just bagged a huge $20 million seed round which they announced last month. It was led by Pantera, with Coinbase Ventures, Variant and Hashed all jumping in too.

I believe this isn't just about chasing the hype around high TPS but about actually making blockchain tech relevant in our daily life.
