Rialo: a blockchain aiming to bridge the gap between Web2 and Web3

Today, we see countless projects in the Web3 space, but not many are truly trying to change the status quo. One exception is Rialo - a team that positions itself not as just another "Layer 1" network, but as a blockchain built for the real world.

Why does this matter?

One of Web3 biggest challenges has always been low user retention. People try out products but quickly leave because of complex wallets, high and unpredictable fees, fragmented identities, and the lack of a familiar user experience.

As a result, Web3 often feels more like an experimental "sandbox for geeks" than an environment for mass adoption.

Rialo wants to change that. Their mission is to eliminate the barrier between Web2 and Web3, make onboarding simple and intuitive, and build decentralized applications that are as seamless as Instagram, Uber, or WhatsApp.

Key innovations of Rialo:

Data and connectivity: smart contracts can access real-world data via HTTPS and APIs.

Identity: support for familiar logins (email, social accounts) and even real-world credentials such as credit scores.

Privacy: confidential yet verifiable execution of transactions.

Speed and scalability: sub-second latency with global reach.

Usability: 2FA, scheduled transactions, and social logins — everything designed to make blockchain invisible to the user.

What does this mean for developers?

Rialo aims to remove the main pain points developers face:

complex off-chain integrations;

reliance on outdated data;

delays caused by slow transaction finality.

My perspective

Personally, I see great potential in this idea. The next generation of users and developers won care about terms like "Layer 1" or "gas fees, nor about the technicalities of Web3. What they will care about is whether an app works smoothly, quickly, and without unnecessary friction. Rialo is building exactly for that future.

Currently, the project is on a private devnet, giving early builders the chance to test features, explore the infrastructure, and join the community. You can get involved through the Rialo website, waitlist, Discord, and social channels.
Perhaps mass adoption of Web3 will begin with approaches like this.

blockchains are closed systems. they can store state, process transactions, and secure assets. but they cannot:

→ react to off-chain events (flight delays, sensor triggers, news updates)

→ schedule future actions (payments, unlocks, renewals)

every time you wanted a blockchain to touch reality, you had to find a way to add middleware on top: oracles, indexers, bots, relayers.
It kept the system alive. but it also bled billions in cost, trust, and fragility.

developers wasted months building brittle integrations.
users stared at stale feeds.
apps broke under load.
attackers found cracks and drained vaults.

this is the “hidden tax” of web3 nobody talks about.

what is Rialo?

👉 Stop outsourcing reality.

Instead of middleware, Rialo makes real-world data, identity, and reactivity protocol-native.

Rialo | Have you ever thought about why we need RWAs (Real World Assets) and why Rialo ?

RWAs (Real-World Assets) in the cryptocurrency and blockchain market are real-world assets such as real estate, commodities, or traditional financial assets, tokenized and put on the blockchain for trading and management. Tokenizing RWAs brings many benefits to both users and blockchain projects, such as:

ㆍ Increased liquidity: Illiquid assets (such as real estate or unlisted stocks) can be easily traded on blockchain exchanges, giving investors access to a wider market and increasing the liquidity of the asset.
ㆍ Shared ownership: Tokenizing RWAs allows for sharing of real-world asset ownership, making large assets easily divided among many investors.
ㆍTransparency and Security: Blockchain provides transparency of ownership and transaction history of assets, reducing the risk of fraud and facilitating safer transactions.
ㆍReduce transaction costs: The use of smart contracts reduces intermediary costs and traditional transaction fees, while automating many processes.

🚀Regarding Rialo, this project can solve the problem of tokenizing RWAs through a system that supports the transfer and trading of real-world assets on the blockchain. Rialo can provide tools and mechanisms to help:

﹒Tokenize assets: Rialo helps convert real-world assets into tokens on the blockchain.
﹒Asset value assurance: Rialo verifies and secures tokenized assets so that they have real-world value.

I’ve been watching new blockchains emerge for a long time. Most of them looked the same: the same promises of speed, security, and scalability. But deep down, I was always looking for something different — something that would truly connect the blockchain world with reality, with our everyday lives.

Then I came across Rialo (@RialoHQ) — a Layer 1 blockchain that boldly calls itself the “Real-World Blockchain.” Created by Subzero Labs, it tackles crypto’s biggest headache: dApps being isolated from the real world. Instead of static assets like a simple NFT or PDF, Rialo turns them into “living assets” that react to real-world events — interest rate changes, market dips, or even bank payments.

To me, this felt absolutely groundbreaking.

First, Rialo gives developers the chance to avoid spending months orchestrating oracles, bridges, or APIs. They say it cuts this process by 80%.

Second, it’s a real breakthrough for tokenizing real-world assets: from government bonds to real estate and insurance, which can now update automatically.

And importantly, Rialo focuses on a Web2-like user experience: fast, low-cost, and secure — like familiar internet services, only powered by Web3.

The tech side is equally impressive. Rialo is a full-stack system independent of Ethereum or Solana.

Real-world events can directly trigger smart contracts.

Web2/API data integrates natively via webhooks.

DAG architecture allows parallel transactions, with RISC-V and even Solana VM compatibility.

It also supports ZK proofs, private and public network connections, and regulatory compliance.

When I started learning more about the team, any doubts vanished. The founders are engineers from Netflix, AMD, Mysten Labs, Meta, and Google. Among them are Ade Adepoju and Lu Zhang, people who have built systems at global scale. The team also includes experts from Apple, Coinbase, Polkadot, and Solana — not just a team, but a true infrastructure-level “dream team.”

Even more confidence came from funding: in August 2025, Rialo raised $20 million in a Seed round from Pantera Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Hashed, Variant, and others. Not every startup can boast such a background.

The community is thriving as well: over 170,000 members on Discord, active quests, gamification, regular posts on X, and #Rialo trending in Asia. The energy there is truly electric.

And here’s what I realized: Rialo is not just another L1. It could be the bridge connecting Web2 and Web3. At a time when RWAs are the big trend and traditional giants like BlackRock are entering crypto, Rialo has the potential to become the platform for DeFi 2.0.

For me, this isn’t just a project. It’s a chance to see blockchain finally become part of the real world.

Big news from @zama_fhe, bootstrapping in under 1 millisecond.

For context: bootstrapping is the “noise cleaning” step in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE), and it used to be the main bottleneck. 
In 2021 it took 53ms. Today? 0.9ms. That’s a 56x speedup. 🤯

Arithmetic on encrypted data is now blazing fast too:
       •  64-bit addition: 2,000ms → 8.7ms (230x faster)
       •  64-bit multiplication: 13,000ms → 32ms (400x faster)

What this means in practice: confidential stablecoin transfers jumped from 0.1 tps (2022) to 230 tps today, faster than Ethereum and most L2s. And this is just the beginning.

Next up: an FHE ASIC that could push 100k tps by 2029. That’s enough to handle Visa, Mastercard, and SWIFT volume combined.

💡Note: FHE just went from “theoretical and too slow” → “production-ready and game-changing.” Privacy at scale is finally real.

Rialo - making the internet and blockchain work together
In plain words: when something happens in your service (an order is placed, a subscription is paid, a ticket is scanned), Rialo can instantly record it on-chain and trigger the right action. No duct tape, no long delays.

Why does this matter?
- So important events aren’t lost or altered.
- So things run faster and more transparently: happened-recorded-action.
- So you rely less on custom bots and fragile scripts.

How it works (super short):
- An event happens in a normal web service/site.
- That service sends a simple "notification" to the network.
- The network immediately runs the required action and leaves a proof on the blockchain.

A few everyday examples:
- Online store: order status changes-the new stage/guarantee is recorded onchain and the next step runs automatically.
- Subscriptions: payment is confirmed-access turns on, with a transparent onchain record.
- Tickets / events: QR is scanned at the door-access is confirmed on-chain, fewer disputes.

Why it’s better than the old way:
Old way: event-your server-custom script-something gets stuck-manual fix.
With Rialo: the event goes straight to the network and is recorded. Less manual work, fewer hidden moving parts.

Who benefits:
- Online services and shops.
- Platforms with access/permissions.
- Any project where "what happened on the regular internet" should be reflected onchain immediately and honestly.

Key idea:
Rialo is about a clean, direct Web2/Web3 link so real business processes run simpler and more reliably.

Bottom line:
@RialoHQ is a straightforward bridge: internet event-onchain action. Transparent and fast.

Real-world assets (RWAs): tokenized bonds, real estate, invoices, insurance contracts, commodities, have long held immense promise for blockchain. Yet they often fall flat: slow, disconnected, and static. @RialoHQ  is here to change that.

Here's why traditional RWAs don’t live up to the hype

Most rely on off-chain verification: dividends, stock splits, and buyouts require manual checks before updating on-chain.

They’re sluggish and reactive: market-moving events like natural disasters or credit downgrades may take hours or days to reflect.

RWAs often lack live data feeds, so they don’t auto-adjust to changes in inflation, appraisals, zoning, or other key metrics.

Automation is limited: settlement, rebalancing, and repricing often require human intervention.

If RWAs stay this way, the expected $30 trillion RWA market by 2030 will just mirror the old system—without any upgrade.

Rialo: Making RWAs Truly Real

From Static Tokens to Living Assets

Every Rialo-enabled RWA shares the same transformative DNA:

1. Live Data Feeds embedded inside.

2. Automated On-Chain Reactions to a changing real world.

3. Seamless Connection to external systems and stakeholders.

You know, I've been deep in the crypto trenches, researching projects until my eyes felt like they were powered by a faulty ASIC. And then I stumbled upon @RialoHQ. Now, I've seen a lot of projects try to reinvent the wheel, or worse, reinvent a square wheel and call it revolutionary. But Rialo? They're trying to build a car, but with the ambition of making it fly... and have a built-in coffee maker. 🚀☕️

Seriously though, imagine a world where your decentralized applications (dApps) aren't just stuck in their own little blockchain silos. It's like having a bunch of super-smart robots, but they can only talk to other robots in their own factory. @RialoHQ is aiming to be the universal translator, the inter-dimensional portal for your dApps. They're building a cross-chain interoperability solution that's so advanced, it makes your grandma's dial-up modem look like a quantum entanglement communicator.

Think about it. Right now, moving assets or data between blockchains is about as easy as trying to teach a cat to herd sheep. It’s possible, I guess, but you’ll probably lose a few fingers (or private keys) in the process. Rialo is trying to make it as smooth as butter on a hot Bitcoin. They’re enabling seamless communication and asset transfers across different blockchains, which, let’s be honest, is the crypto equivalent of finally figuring out how to fold a fitted sheet. It’s a game-changer.

Why should you care? 
Because if your favorite dApp can suddenly talk to all the other dApps, no matter their blockchain address, suddenly the possibilities explode. It’s like the internet before interoperability – a bunch of isolated networks. Then BAM! TCP/IP. That's the kind of revolution @RialoHQ is brewing. They're not just building another blockchain; they're building the highways between the blockchains.
So, while others are busy creating the next moonshot meme coin that will evaporate faster than a free donut at a crypto conference, @RialoHQ is laying the groundwork for a truly interconnected decentralized future. It’s complex, ambitious, and frankly, a little bit insane. But in crypto, “a little bit insane” is often just a polite way of saying “brilliant.” Keep an eye on these guys; they might just be the ones to finally get our dApps to play nicely together. And who knows, maybe they’ll even build that flying car with the coffee maker.

full_text:
Developers need a foundation that makes Web3 feel as smooth as Web2 without sacrificing decentralization.

Rialo emerges as a supermodular blockchain built for real-world applications.
But what does that actually mean for developers?

1. Native Real-World Data

Imagine pulling weather data, stock prices, or IoT sensor readings directly into a smart contract.
On other chains, you’d need complex oracles and extra layers.
On Rialo, contracts can call HTTPS or webhooks directly. Real-time data flows on-chain without the overhead.

2. Dual VM Power

Most blockchains lock you into a single virtual machine, limiting your options.
Rialo gives you two:

• RISC-V for flexibility, supporting languages like Rust, C, and Go.

• Solana VM for high-speed parallel execution, handling thousands of transactions per second.
The result: flexibility and performance combined in one chain.

3. Web2 → Web3 Made Easy

Web3 often feels painful: complicated gas fees, high latency, unfamiliar tooling.
Rialo makes it familiar: low latency, modular design, and developer-friendly tools.
For Web2 developers, the transition to Web3 feels natural without breaking your workflow.

Rialo isn’t just another blockchain.
It’s the foundation that lets developers focus on building products instead of fighting infrastructure.

Want to dive deeper?
Check the official website or join the developer community on Discord to connect directly with the team and other builders.

full_text:
Current L1s have the same UX friction as Symbian - high gas fees create "button-limited" thinking where developers optimize for transaction minimalism.

Most scaling solutions still miss the point, L2s are like better smartphone keyboards - cheaper transactions but same paradigm. Developers still think of "expensive database operations" instead of building rich apps.
App-specific rollups are the real iPhone moment, purpose-built chains for gaming, social, and DeFi that optimize their entire stack for specific use cases rather than one-size-fits-all limitations.

Shared sequencing/interoperability creates the "app store infrastructure" where users don't think about which chain they're on, just like they don't think about servers when using apps.

The breakthrough isn't making Ethereum faster, it's rethinking the stack entirely. We need application-optimized platforms, not general "world computers" treating everything as database problems.

We're transitioning: Palm Pilot (monolithic L1s) → Symbian (current L2s) → iPhone (app-specific rollups).

How to Get Attention on @RialoHQ.

What Qualifies as High-Quality Content for Rialo and How to Start Building Your Mindshare Early.

Let’s be honest, there is TOO MUCH of crypto content everywhere -threads, graphics, endless Discord messages, "alpha from KOLs", and "InfoFi AI garbage". 

Most people lose interest fast to the project.

So, how can we make people care about what we do?

> CHAPTER 1: INFOFI META

Right now, "infoFi" is likely the most important tool for marketing Web3 projects. Platforms like @KaitoAI and @wallchain_xyz are popular, and almost all the latest prominent projects are joining the InfoFi space. 

Projects based in the US are especially eager to participate. The latest examples - @MagicNewton, @MMTFinance, @JoinSapien, and @0G_labs, to name just a few.

⭐️NOTE 1: As you can see @RialoHQ is the project with a strong marketing team and it based in the US. There is a  very high probability that Rialo will join InfoFi narrative.

What it means for us?

If you start building your reputation on Rialo now in X, Kaito algos will build your Mindshare before the crowd (Especially KOLS) come into Rialo "yapping" or "quacking".

This is exactly what happened to me when I started talking about @MagicNewton five months before Kaito. It helped me make a five figure income.

> CHAPTER 2: HOW TO BUILD MINDSHARE FOR RIALO

So, what is high-quality content on Rialo? The answer: content that people remember and want to share. Here’s how you can create it.

1. Teach Something Useful

> Don’t make your content boring. Don’t just copy from the website or repeat the basics. Go deeper.

> Explain Simply: What is special about Rialo? Explain clearly and use examples. Avoid hard words and long sentences.
(example - https://t.co/DsGL545m6b)

> Show How Things Work: Talk about Rialo important features. Show how you use the platform (ofc when testnet/devnet is launched)

> Give Real Tips: Share easy guides and step-by-step tutorials. Show screenshots so it’s easy to understand.

2. Share Your Own Ideas

> Give New Insights: Find something unique by using Rialo. Share your process and results. Share Screenshots of dashboard.

> Compare Fairly: How is Rialo different from other platforms who builds the similar products? Be honest - what is good and what needs work?

> Think About the Future: How could Rialo help normal users or big companies in the future? Share your ideas.

3. Show, Don’t Just Tell

⭐️NOTE 2: It’s easier to learn with pictures or jokes.

> Show Your Work: Give case studies. Use charts and real examples from your research.

> Use Visuals: Make simple and clear graphics to explain ideas.

> Memes Are Great: Make funny pictures or jokes about using Rialo. Humor helps people learn and remember.

4. Be Active in the Community

⭐️NOTE 3: Building your reputation means talking with people, not just sharing posts.

> Join the Discussion: Ask questions. Give real answers. Help new users understand Rialo.

> Support Others: Share good content from the Rialo community. Work with others.

> Tell Your Story: Share why you joined Rialo and what you have learned. Honest stories connect people!

5. Promote your Content 

> Again Support: When you just posted your content on X, make sure you asked your friends on Discord to like and reply what you just dropped.

> Community on X: Show your posts to people who already interested on your content. You will quickly get replies and likes if you post your content through specific community on X. 

⭐️NOTE 4: We already created the most supportive Rialo Club community, welcome to join - https://t.co/ypruXCvQkC

In short:

Start early. Make smart, clear content. The time you spend building your name now will help you stand out when @RialoHQ grows. 

⭐️NOTE 5: Be the voice people listen to, not just another user.

In crypto, if people forget about you, you disappear. 

Don’t let that happen, make your content matter.

P.S. If you find helpful my article and you liked it, your Like and Reply is the best token of appreciation. But your retweet means a "Burj Khalifa" for me! 🤣

6 things you probably didn’t know about @RialoHQ and why it actually matters 👀 

Web3 today feels like a collection of bubbles. Complicated wallets, seed phrases, bots, gas wars, endless middleware. Normal people don’t want that. They just want apps that connect with the real world and just work. That’s exactly where Rialo steps in.

If you haven’t discovered it yet, we’re waiting for you in the Rialo Discord. Come see what’s being built 👇 
https://t.co/URKgy4SBvP

1. 🌦 Real-world info onchain
Picture this: an app checks the weather forecast and automatically adjusts your transactions depending on whether it rains or shines. With Rialo’s native HTTPS integration, dApps can connect directly with APIs from the real world — weather, credit scores, payments, social platforms — without messy oracles or fragile middleware. It’s simple, direct, and powerful.

2. 📦 Real-time reactions
Web3 apps today don’t really react on their own — you need bots or constant monitoring. With Rialo, transactions can fire automatically when something happens in real life: your delivery is confirmed, a market price changes, or a trigger condition is met. That means no more babysitting positions or praying your bot doesn’t fail.

3. 💸 DeFi that feels like a banking app
DeFi right now is complex and fragile. With Rialo, your staking position can automatically restake when the APY changes, or your collateral can be topped up before liquidation. Even copy-trading becomes native and real-time. No more bots, no scripts, no middlemen. Just seamless automation built into the chain itself.

4. 👨‍💻 Web2 builders, welcome
Developers from outside crypto often give up because tools feel alien. Rialo solves that with support for RISC-V and Solana VM. This means code from Web2 or Solana can be ported with little effort. Builders get a familiar environment, less friction, and faster shipping. Rialo feels like home for devs, but with all the power of Web3.

5. 🕶 Smooth and invisible UX
Nobody wants to see “please wait…” while a transaction crawls. On Rialo, the infrastructure is invisible: fast, private, reactive. Apps run smoothly like the ones people already use every day — WhatsApp, Uber, Netflix. You don’t feel the blockchain, but you get its security and transparency in the background.

6. 🚀 Applications that finally make sense
Because of this full-stack, event-driven design, Rialo unlocks things that just weren’t possible before: tokenization of real-world assets, AI agents that act instantly, ultra-responsive prediction markets, apps that mix Web2 simplicity with Web3 transparency. The kind of apps people would actually use in real life — not just speculation.

👉 Rialo isn’t about about real usability + real world integration. It’s the blockchain that finally feels like it was made for everyday people
